text: Indian oil sardine (Sardinella longiceps) is under a seasonal closure. Configured closure months: June and July. Reason: spawning protection - monsoon fishing closure. During these months the advisory for this species is STOP (DO NOT FISH) regardless of weather or how likely the fish are: conservation rules run before any scoring. This entry is deployment-configured, not an official legal text: verify it against the managing authority's current notification before relying on it.
source: config.yaml (deployment closure registry)

text: The advisory has four classes, from the configured thresholds: PROCEED when the index is at or above 0.75 (GO); PROCEED WITH CAUTION when the index is at or above 0.6 (GO CAREFULLY); DELAY OR RELOCATE when the index is at or above 0.4 (WAIT OR MOVE); DO NOT FISH below 0.4, or whenever a hard constraint applies. The class is computed by the deterministic rules engine and scoring, never by the AI assistant, and the assistant may not contradict it.
source: advisory configuration + rules engine

text: The sustainability index is a weighted sum of catch likelihood (0.45), weather safety (0.25) and the ecological term (0.3). It is monotonic in every input, the weights are configuration owned by governance rather than hidden constants, and a protected area or closure overrides the score entirely.
source: advisory configuration + scoring engine

text: Protected areas and seasonal closures are enforced as hard, fail-closed constraints: if the registry is unreachable the request is refused rather than cleared, so an outage can never produce a permissive answer. This is why a STOP may appear with the reason 'MPA registry unavailable' - it is the conservation guard working as designed, not a fault.
source: rules engine (fail-closed guard)

text: What the assistant will and will not do: it summarises the advisory in plain language, answers questions using the advisory data plus retrieved passages and cites them, and reads catch photos, satellite tiles and charts describing only what is visible. It never overrules the advisory class, never softens a STOP, refuses rather than invents when it has no retrieved context, and always names the backend and model that produced an answer.
source: assistant layer documentation

text: Weather safety in the advisory is judged from live marine and meteorological forecasts - wind speed and gusts, wave height, wave period and direction - against the limits of small boats. Calm conditions raise the safety component and rough conditions lower it, so an advisory can be WAIT OR MOVE even where fish are likely. Warnings apply to the requested point, not to a whole district: conditions a few kilometres offshore differ from the harbour, and they change through the day.
source: advisory system documentation (weather-safety component)

text: Ecological risk in the advisory covers bycatch and habitat harm: it rises near sensitive habitats such as seagrass, coral and mangroves, and during juvenile recruitment months, and it lowers the final class even when catch likelihood is high. The rule the system encodes is that catching the target fish does not justify damaging the nursery grounds the next season depends on.
source: advisory system documentation (bycatch / ecological term)

text: Monsoon fishing ban: rest for the sea, new life for the fishery. During Kerala's annual monsoon fishing closure, fish spawning is protected. ICAR-CMFRI continuously monitors landings after the ban and asks fishers to follow weather warnings.
source: regional ocean news seed (Kerala, India; source: ICAR-CMFRI)

text: Coral reefs and seagrass protection gains strength in the Gulf of Mannar. In the Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve, work continues to restore coral reefs, seagrass beds and turtle habitats. Sustainable fishing practices are being promoted together with local fisher associations.
source: regional ocean news seed (Tamil Nadu, India; source: Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve)

text: Mangrove restoration in the Sundarbans: a strong wall of coastal protection. The Sundarbans mangrove forests shield coastal villages from storms and serve as fish breeding grounds. Restoration programmes are encouraging local fishing communities to take part in nurseries and plantation work.
source: regional ocean news seed (West Bengal, India; source: National Mangrove Initiative)

text: Satellite fishing-zone advisories reach more small-scale fishers. The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services continues to issue Potential Fishing Zone advisories derived from sea-surface-temperature and chlorophyll fronts. Delivery over mobile phones has widened reach among small-scale fishers, helping cut search time and fuel spend.
source: regional ocean news seed (India; source: INCOIS)

text: Indian Ocean tuna stocks under continued management review. The Indian Ocean Tuna Commission's scientific committees keep assessing yellowfin, skipjack and bigeye stocks as fishing pressure and market demand grow. Management measures and catch limits are reviewed against the latest stock assessments, with coastal-state livelihoods a standing concern.
source: regional ocean news seed (Indian Ocean; source: IOTC)

text: Ocean heat content keeps climbing, scientists warn. Global ocean heat content continues its long-term rise, driving marine heatwaves, coral stress and shifts in fish distributions. Monitoring agencies emphasise that coastal communities depending on small pelagic fisheries are among the first to feel the effects.
source: regional ocean news seed (Global; source: NOAA / WMO)

text: Global plastics treaty talks continue to protect the ocean. Negotiations toward a legally binding global plastics agreement continue, with marine pollution at the centre. Roughly eleven million tonnes of plastic still enter the ocean every year, and coastal fisheries report growing amounts of debris in nets and gear.
source: regional ocean news seed (Global; source: UNEP)

text: Small-scale fisheries gain recognition in food-security policy. Global assessments continue to highlight that small-scale fisheries supply a large share of fish consumed in developing regions and support hundreds of millions of livelihoods. Voluntary guidelines push for secure tenure, social protection and market access for small-scale fishers.
source: regional ocean news seed (Global; source: FAO)
